title: The Solution Brief and G3: what will be built and the bar it must meet, signed before training and judged once at the holdout
request: Phase 8 (the owner's framework, phase 3): a brief with the approach level, the recipe, the baselines, the validation, the success bar, the decision rule, the risks and the alternatives; refused without a bar, a baseline or an alternative; the bar frozen at a signature and the holdout's verdict against it in the report. Decision D3: a signed brief covers the holdout approval.
plan: Write the contract in the library, with G3, a signature over a fingerprint and a judge that reads the holdout once.
Draft a brief by rules from what the engine prepares, never from holdout rows.
Sign it with the solution gate, let a signed brief stand for the agent's holdout approval, and judge the bar at the final stage.
Say the verdict in the report, from the record, and give the brief two routes.

decisions.decision: The default bar is better than the recipe's simple model on the primary metric; for recall at a review budget, better than reviewing that share at random.
decisions.why: It is the honest least a model must clear, it can always be judged from the holdout's own baselines, and a person raises it before signing.

decisions.decision: A brief is saved through the graph's own move, set_brief: a person only, never while a stage runs, never after the holdout read.
decisions.why: The bar must be fixed before the one read; a change under a running final or after it would be chosen on the holdout.

decisions.decision: D3 holds only while the brief and the solution are both signed and unchanged, and not for a programme.
decisions.why: A signed brief over a changed solution says nothing about what is now run; a programme judges no bar.

decisions.decision: A brief is stored only when a person saves one; the solution gate does not draft and sign one unseen.
decisions.why: A signature means the person agreed the bar; signing a rule's draft nobody read would also make D3 remove the holdout gate silently. Sign-off on by default is left to the owner.

decisions.decision: Metric directions and what the engine's simple models report are named in the library.
decisions.why: G3 must refuse a bar that goes the wrong way or could never be judged, and the library never imports the studio.

change: dclab_core.solution_brief (SolutionBrief v1, LADDER, Baseline with today's number, Guard, SuccessBar, Approval, HIGHER, REPORTS, fingerprint, problems, signed, sign, fill, BarVerdict, judge); dclab_core.report's verdict line; dclab_rnd.studio.brief (draft for tabular and machine kinds, view, save, verdict_of); the graph's set_brief move, brief_problems, brief_signed and the solution gate's signature; the engine's success_bar in both final paths; GET and PUT /api/projects/{id}/brief; the audit kind brief and its decision.accepted event; dclab-core 0.90.0.

findings.defect: The brief's save named an audit kind the trail does not have.
findings.cause: A new kind used before it was declared.
findings.fix: The kind brief declared, with its event (point solution.brief) and its filter on the Admin page.

findings.defect: A bar could be moved after the holdout read and then signed.
findings.scenario: Sign, start the final, PUT a margin of -0.5, the final completes, approve the solution gate again: the moved bar signed, a rerun judged on it.
findings.cause: The save checked only the count of holdout reads, written at the end of the final; the gate signed whatever brief was stored.
findings.fix: The save is the graph's set_brief move (refused while a stage runs and after a read); the gate never signs a brief after a read.

findings.defect: D3 let an agent read the holdout after the solution changed.
findings.scenario: Sign the solution and the brief, change the solution, require the holdout approval: the agent's final was allowed.
findings.cause: brief_signed read only the brief's own fingerprint.
findings.fix: brief_signed also needs the gate's brief hash and the solution signed; programmes keep their own holdout approval.

findings.defect: Kinds with their own machine crashed the brief and were never judged.
findings.scenario: GET the brief of an anomaly or forecasting project: AttributeError, 500; its final wrote no verdict.
findings.cause: The draft read the tabular bundle's spec; only the tabular final judged the bar.
findings.fix: A machine's metric, direction and own first baseline; its final judged against its own baselines.

findings.defect: G3 passed bars that could never be judged.
findings.scenario: Recall at the budget against the majority class; a bar against today's process with no number; a misspelt metric against a simple model.
findings.cause: G3 checked only that a target and a named baseline existed.
findings.fix: An absolute bar for recall at the budget, today's number on the baseline, a relative bar only on a metric the simple model reports.

findings.defect: judge gave wrong verdicts on guards and on direction.
findings.scenario: An mae above the baseline judged met under op '>'; an rmse guard with the default op failed when better; a guard with no target failed; a missing guard metric failed.
findings.cause: No direction check, no alias for guards, a missing value read as failure.
findings.fix: G3 refuses comparisons against a metric's direction and guards without a target or a named baseline; judge reads guards as the bar and says cannot be judged when a guard cannot be read.

findings.defect: D3 and G3 apply only to a project whose brief a person saved.
findings.scenario: No page saves a brief yet; the solution gate signs without one.
findings.fix: Kept opt-in (decision above) and left to the owner with the Solution page's editor.

findings.defect: Saving the brief bypassed the validator.
findings.scenario: No graph check, no transition logged for a state change.
findings.fix: The set_brief move, checked and logged.

findings.defect: The report could say a bar was not met without the reason.
findings.scenario: The primary metric above its target and a guard failed.
findings.fix: The failed guards named, their numbers from the record.

findings.defect: A value that is not finite crashed the final after the holdout was read.
findings.fix: Cannot be judged, and the stage stands.

findings.defect: The audit recorded a role, not the person.
findings.scenario: The row said Owner, not who.
findings.cause: The role used for the name.
findings.fix: The approver's name, as the approvals route records it.

findings.defect: The refusal promised a way out that does not exist.
findings.scenario: A later period or new rows: the count never resets.
findings.fix: A new bar needs a new holdout: a new project on later rows.

findings.defect: The capture was not read back and several paths were untested.
findings.scenario: No test of the audit row or the event; none for machines, budgets, guards, a sign after the read, a changed solution.
findings.cause: Tests of the main path only.

measurements.name: the harness suite on the rules
measurements.gate: 21.5: a change to the validator is on only after the suite passes
measurements.against_gate: Every written case and dev journey right on every step and part.

outcome: A brief says what will be built and the bar it must meet; it cannot be signed incomplete, cannot move after the one holdout read, and the report says whether the bar was met.
lessons: A value frozen at a signature must be closed to edits by the validator, not by a check of a counter written at the end of the run it guards.
A shortcut that stands in for an approval must hold only while everything the approval covered is unchanged.
risks: A brief exists only when a person saves one; the Solution page's editor, sign-off on by default, a model drafting the words and the main product's Objective are left.
